results.comment: It took until almost the end of the conversation for the energy cost of mining to come up. About 3:35. Can't say I found the the answer M.S. provided very convincing. As I understood it, he was comparing the energy efficiency of Bitcoin mining to industrial operations like auto manufacturing or steel production. But how are these even comparable? I can drive a car and make a roof out of steel. I think a fairer comparison, since Bitcoin is an asset comparable to gold would be an energy comparison of gold mining to Bitcoin mining. But even in that case, I can buy my sweetheart a gold ring and we can use gold in electronics manufacture and other industrial applications. Seems to me the fairest comparison would be with the energy costs of other financial transaction processes: clearing a credit card purchase, conducting a wire transfer, etc. I'm not convinced those comparisons would be very favourable.
